nodes.label: Core safety contract
nodes.rationale: IBKR is treated as sole authority for contracts/quotes/positions/orders; durable idempotency keys and pre-placeOrder evidence commits exist so a crash or ambiguous ack never causes a silent duplicate or unrecoverable order.

nodes.label: Deliberate limits and readiness blockers
nodes.rationale: Adapter deliberately withholds a claim of production readiness until API/TWS version pinning, market-data entitlement verification, and restart drills are complete; unknown submissions are quarantined, not auto-resolved.

nodes.label: Old sizing/scale-out explicitly not ported
nodes.rationale: The old app's risk-cap sizing (up to 50 contracts) and scale-out/stop management directly conflict with core/config.py's hard max_contracts_per_order==1 cap and require an execution/fill/protection ledger this slice doesn't yet have; porting them would silently violate the 'automated closes not implemented' invariant.

nodes.label: Electron renderer security boundary
nodes.rationale: contextIsolation, sandboxing, and disabled nodeIntegration keep the renderer from touching Electron/Node/filesystem/IBKR credentials directly, so a compromised or malicious web page cannot reach the broker connection.

nodes.label: Manual recovery procedure
nodes.rationale: When the app can't verify a position/quantity, the operator resolves it directly in TWS rather than letting the app auto-close or cancel a manual/external order — automated interpretation of unverified state is treated as unsafe.

nodes.label: Safety invariants (1-10)
nodes.rationale: Enumerates why persistence-before-broker-call, single durable order attempt, SUBMISSION_UNKNOWN non-retry, and account/environment cross-checks exist: to make a duplicate order or silent live-flip structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged.

nodes.label: Live trading opt-in
nodes.rationale: Live is deliberately gated behind an exact confirmation phrase, a separate live allowlist, standard live ports, and a two-sided session/config environment cross-check so no UI action or code path can silently flip an account from paper to live.

nodes.label: Deliberate deferrals
nodes.rationale: Bracket/partial-fill protection claims, multi-account/FA, spreads, short premium, hosted ingress, and signed/notarized release gates are explicitly out of scope for this slice rather than silently unimplemented — each requires separate implementation and validation.

nodes.label: Tauri WKWebView security boundary
nodes.rationale: Chosen as a lighter (~5-10MB binary) alternative to Electron while keeping identical safety boundaries: loopback-only origins, isolated WKWebView context, strict CSP, no direct filesystem/IPC access.

nodes.label: Hardcoded scope limit: no order can currently reach IBKR from a webhook alert
nodes.rationale: Doc states APP_MANAGEMENT_EXECUTION_AVAILABLE = false is a hardcoded scope limit in server.mjs, not a config flag, so a TradingView webhook alert can never place an IBKR order today in any QT_TRADING_MODE — set up alerts to validate ingestion/dedup only.
